metrics.tasks: sessions whose updatedAt falls within the period
metrics.messages: total TurnRecord count across those sessions (session-level period attribution, documented simplification)
metrics.tokens: sum of run_inspection.usage.totalTokens for those sessions; UI labels this 'Tokens (agent runs)' since ordinary chat turns have no token accounting
metrics.activeDays: distinct calendar dates from turn completedAt/startedAt (fallback session.updatedAt) within the period
metrics.currentStreak: lifetime, independent of period filter — confirmed identical across periods in tests
metrics.mostUsedModel: mode of run_inspection.provider.modelId (source=agent-run) falling back to mode of session.currentModelId (source=session-selection); null with hasAnyHistory=false when no data exists

heatmap.definition: one cell per day, level 0/1/2/3 bucketed at 0 / 1-2 / 3-5 / 6+ messages that day

chips.runtime: resolveRuntimeLabel() in model-sections.ts — Auto / Hosted / Direct (BYOK), derived from the real selected model's providerId/tier
chips.workspace: real project name with full path in a tooltip
chips.branch: git-workspace-info.ts classifyGitWorkspace() — single `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD --git-dir --git-common-dir` call; no chip rendered for a non-git directory; detached HEAD shown truthfully
chips.worktree: same git call — detected via --git-dir vs --git-common-dir divergence (the standard git worktree mechanism), shown only when true

composerContextBar.canonicalSourceUnification: desktop header's branch display now reads the same gitInfo object as the context bar

closeProtection.modalBehavior: unchanged, CloseDialog.tsx already correct (Cancel/Quit(-anyway)/Keep running in tray, unrecoverable re-prompt race); now shares summarizeActiveWork() with the tray tooltip
closeProtection.trayIndicator: new — tray tooltip shows 'CodeForge — N workflow(s) · N agent turn(s)...' while work is running (excludes pendingApprovals), refreshed every 15s, reset to 'CodeForge' when idle
closeProtection.persistedPreference: unchanged, already correct (ask/tray/quit-safe, written only for a recoverable choice)

backgroundAgentProof.reason: packaged app cannot get past CodeForgeServer construction due to the native SQLite ABI blocker (see remainingBlockers)
whatWasProven: CodeForgeServer.getRuntimeStatus() accurately reflects a genuinely active task and its completion, using a real server with no mocking of the status computation
code reading confirms the 'tray' decision path never calls server.stop() or app.quit() in either requestClose() or the app:close-decision IPC handler
the packaged app reaches WHEN_READY_WINDOW_CREATED (window created, renderer loaded) before failing at server init for the unrelated native-module reason
backgroundAgentProof.claimNotMade: that an agent literally kept running after minimizing was not directly observed inside a live packaged window

liveUiVerification.method: real production build served and driven in a browser tab against a real CodeForgeServer instance seeded with real session/turn/run_inspection history — not a qa.html mock
confirmed: Overview card real metrics: tasks 9, messages 27, tokens 37.5K, active days 7, streak 3d, most-used model resolved to display name
7d period filter live-recomputed tasks/messages/tokens/active-days while streak and heatmap stayed identical
context bar all four chips real and live-updating (runtime changed Auto->Hosted after model selection)
header branch/worktree badge matches the context bar
Add favorite opens the identical canonical picker; starring a model and closing made it appear as a real favorite chip
sidebar correctly showed seeded session history grouped by recency, confirming no regression to existing features

midSessionBugFixed.symptom: Cannot find module close-lifecycle.js crash reported live by the user
midSessionBugFixed.rootCause: close-lifecycle.ts lived under src/renderer/, whose compiled output directory is emptied by every Vite renderer build, silently deleting the main-process compiled file on a renderer-only rebuild
midSessionBugFixed.fix: moved close-lifecycle.ts to src/ (sibling to main.ts), updated both consumers' imports, added it to the renderer tsconfig's include list for typecheck convenience only
midSessionBugFixed.verifiedFixed: clean rebuild + repackage + smoke test now progresses to the same pre-existing unrelated native-module blocker, no module-not-found crash

testsExecuted.typecheck: clean across packages/ui, apps/desktop (main + renderer), packages/server after every change

buildResult.npmRunBuildNative: FAIL - same pre-existing Visual Studio 2026/node-gyp incompatibility as prior milestone; unrelated to this work

packagedRuntimeResult.launch: PASS - window created, real renderer bundle loaded (WINDOW_CONTENT_LOADED, WHEN_READY_WINDOW_CREATED reached)
packagedRuntimeResult.serverInit: FAIL - better-sqlite3 native binding compiled for plain Node ABI, not Electron 33's ABI (v130); Electron's bundled Node lacks node:sqlite

regressionsChecked.scopeConfirmed: git diff --stat touches only the files in filesChanged
regressionsChecked.fullServerSuitePassing: 487/487 (3 skipped) including CF-09 mission steering/budget/security/recovery/acceptance, publication, network-exposure, workflow terminal-state races

remainingBlockers.description: This machine's Visual Studio 2026 install is incompatible with node-gyp's VS detection, and Electron's bundled Node lacks node:sqlite, so the packaged app cannot get past CodeForgeServer construction to reach a state where a real agent turn and a real minimize-to-tray could be observed inside actual Electron chrome.
remainingBlockers.missingProof: The exact scenario in the milestone spec (start a real task, request close, choose minimize to tray, confirm the process/task survives, restore, confirm completion) run on a toolchain — or CI runner pinned to windows-2022, per this project's existing operational memory — capable of the native rebuild.

remainingBlockers.description: The full packaged-desktop smoke path (launch, open workspace, land on empty state, verify overview/context/model controls, start a task, close/minimize/restore cycle, quit, restart) could not be executed inside real Electron chrome for the same reason.
remainingBlockers.missingProof: Same toolchain requirement as above; live browser verification (documented in this report) substitutes for everything reachable without a real Electron window but is not a substitute for the packaged-app proof the milestone requires.

fakeCertificationAvoided: No claim is made that a real agent survived minimizing inside a live packaged window, since that was not directly observed. The report distinguishes precisely what was proven (server-level runtime-status accuracy, code-level confirmation the tray path never touches server.stop()/app.quit(), live browser verification of every UI surface reachable without Electron) from what remains unverified.
